rachel: heads up — several linux + mac CI shards started failing right after the gcc image bump (gcr.io/redwood-ci/gcc-2026-03-15:11). Error is missing <memory_resource> in multiple CC targets. Example failing snippet below:
```
In file included from third_party/xyz/foo.cc:12:
third_party/xyz/foo.h:5:10: fatal error: 'memory_resource' file not found
#include <memory_resource>
         ^~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
1 error generated.
```
sam: which exact image tag is that? do you have a failing CI link?
rachel: image: gcr.io/redwood-ci/gcc-2026-03-15:11, CI job: https://ci.redwood/example/12345 (presubmit linux-gcc11-1). Affected targets include //libs/storage:storage_core and //third_party/xyz:client. Appears in both mac and linux shards after the roll.
ci-bot: TOOLCHAIN ROLL DETECTED — toolchain-roll/2026-03-15 by @build-bot (PR #4521) rolled base image to gcr.io/redwood-ci/gcc-2026-03-15:11.
lee: memory_resource is from <memory_resource> (C++17). Some libstdc++ versions and images put headers in different places; if the image swapped libc++ vs libstdc++ or the sysroot changed, the header can be missing. Quick repro: run `docker run --rm gcr.io/redwood-ci/gcc-2026-03-15:11 bash -lc "echo '#include <memory_resource>' | g++ -x c++ - -std=gnu++17 -E -v"` to inspect include paths.
maya: can someone bisect the roll? simplest is try prev image tag gcr.io/redwood-ci/gcc-2026-02-20 and see if CI passes. I can try a local container repro too: `bazel build //libs/storage:storage_core --config=linux-gcc11 --cxxopt='-std=gnu++17' --sandbox_debug`.
rachel: thanks. if reproduces locally, we can either pin presubmit to the previous image or add a toolchain shim to expose the headers. For immediate unblock — @sam can we pin presubmit to the prior image for a few hours?
sam: fine with a temporary pin for presubmit. I will open a small PR to the CI config to set image to gcr.io/redwood-ci/gcc-2026-02-20 for presubmit shards, mark it as hotfix.
rachel: opening a bisect task and assigning to @maya and @lee to confirm reproduction and optionally try a minimal patch (add explicit include path or install libstdc++-dev) — will update thread. please react if you hit the same failure. :thumbsup:
